_note: One sentence per gallery screenshot, keyed by app and gallery label. Shown under the large screenshot on each app page.

Timing.Live race: A race in full swing on your own race screen: race clock, laps to go, start lights, lap times, gaps and the last laps. The race bar shows when the race was last saved.
Timing.Swap Seats: Swap Seats: every lane keeps its own car and the drivers move from lane to lane. Between the heats, the line-up shows who gets into which car.
Timing.Second screen: Before a race, the second screen shows Home for the audience: the next race, its line-up and your cards. Press Start race and it switches to race timing by itself.
Timing.Race setup: Pick a race setup and put a driver and car in every lane, or let Draw lanes decide by lot. Then start the race.
Timing.Lane cars: The results of a Swap Seats race name the car in every heat, and Lane cars shows the laps and best lap of every car, and who drove it.
Timing.Results: The Race Director’s final check: review every lap, adjust or disqualify, then finalise the result.
Timing.Fuel: Set the tank, the fuel used per lap and the refuelling speed, and see straight away how many laps a full tank lasts.
Timing.Weather: Plan when the rain comes and goes, see the forecast at a glance, and set what the wrong tyres cost.
Timing.Widget Builder: Build your own race-screen widgets from text, values and pictures, with a live preview of the race screen.

Paddock.Showroom: Your favourite cars, presented the way they deserve.
Paddock.Car collection: Every car in one place, with photos, specifications and quick filters.
Paddock.Parts catalogue: Keep motors, gears, magnets and every other part organised and easy to find.
Paddock.Wheels & tyres: Browse every wheel and tyre by size, compound and maker, and see what you have in stock.
Paddock.Shopping lists: Know what to buy next, and what you already have.
Paddock.Build from Scratch: Plan a new build, part by part, before it hits the track.
Paddock.Workshop: See every open workshop job at a glance, with the car it belongs to.
Paddock.Workshop job: Record a job step by step: what changed, which parts and why.
Paddock.Import & export: Bring cars in from spreadsheets or files, share selected cars, and keep complete backups.
Paddock.Appearance: Make Paddock your own with a choice of colour themes.

Circuit.Track builder: Lay out a multi-lane track piece by piece, with the parts list, track overview and power marks always in view.
Circuit.Power taps: Mark the power base, let Circuit suggest extra taps and see every stretch between feeds checked as you build.
Circuit.Power test sheet: Enter the voltages you measure on the real track. A lane more than 1 V down is marked.
Circuit.Live Preview: Watch cars lap your design before you build a single piece.
Circuit.Routed track: Design a routed wooden track with flowing curves on a fixed table.
Circuit.FreeForm: Draw one lane freely and let Circuit generate the others, with editable points.
Circuit.Measure & check: Check footprint, lane lengths, gaps and curves before you build.
Circuit.Table Designer: Split your table into transport panels and plan them onto sheets of wood.
Circuit.Import & export: Export your layout as a track file, PDF report, picture, parts list or drawing.

Telemetry.Workbench: Enter your setup and see what each change does as you type.
Telemetry.Setup analysis: Read a saved setup’s numbers: gearing, speed, torque and power.
Telemetry.Compare setups: Put two setups next to each other and spot what really made the difference.
Telemetry.Setup library: Keep every setup you have tried, searchable and ready to reuse.
Telemetry.Lap analysis: Dig into lap times, spread and the laps that cost you most.
Telemetry.Progress: Every lap of every run on one wall, with your record and how much pace you have gained.
Telemetry.Driver Feedback: Describe how the car feels and get suggested checks to try next.
Telemetry.Ballast planner: Plan where weight goes and what it does to the balance of the car.
Telemetry.Tyre wear & clearance: Keep an eye on tyre wear and ground clearance before they cost you laps.

Livery.Design studio: Paint stripes, numbers and sponsors on your car, with every layer editable.
Livery.Decals & race numbers: Fit decals and race numbers onto the body, skewed to match the angle of the car.
Livery.Gradients & stripes: Multi-stop gradients and stripe tools for a paint job that stands out.
Livery.Template preparation: Turn any car drawing into a paintable template: pick the panels that get paint and group them into parts.
Livery.User Library: Keep your decals, stripes and shapes in the Garage, ready for the next design.
Livery.Workshop notes: Paint references and masking steps go along with the design and into the PDF.
Livery.Transparent PNG: Export a finished car as a transparent image for posters, websites or entry lists.
Livery.Welcome: Start a new livery, open a project or pick up where you left off.

Decals.Sheet editor: A full A4 sheet of decals at true model size, with layers, rulers and margins.
Decals.Racing graphics: Curved lettering, number plates and racing stripes, all editable.
Decals.Car preview: Place decals on the side and top of the car at their printed size before you print.
Decals.Vector tracing: Turn a logo into clean, flat-colour shapes as you import it.
Decals.Slice & export: Cut out part of a sheet to print on its own or save to your library.
Decals.Decal library: Save decals to your library, tag them and find favourites again in seconds.
Decals.Scale conversion: Convert a whole sheet between scales, for example 1:32 to 1:24.
Decals.Print & white ink: Print on clear or white decal paper, with white ink behind light colours.

Foundry.Buildings: Race HQ, made from the standard Race headquarters: ready to print, or to change wall by wall. New in Foundry 1.7.
Foundry.Layout with buildings: An oval with fenced advertising boards, and two of your buildings standing beside the track.
Foundry.Trackside: A corner with cobbles cut into the road and advertising boards with catch fences plugged into its edges.
Foundry.Draw a building: Draw the footprint wall by wall: drag a wall in or out, pull out a bay or cut a corner at 45°.
Foundry.Lettering and finishes: The Container café, with a container shell and lettering on its sign.
Foundry.New track pack: Make a pack step by step. Only Basics is needed; road, borders, lines, road surface and trackside are optional.
Foundry.Turnout: A single-lane turnout with a moving blade, worked by a motor under the road.
Foundry.STL Edit: Edit, cut and repair STL models, from a small tool to a fix on someone else’s part.
Foundry.Home: Start a new pack or a new building, and reopen your recent layouts and buildings.

Anvil.Clearance: Bigger tyres? Anvil shows in red where the body comes too close, with a button to cut the arches.
Anvil.Shell: Cut the underside open at a floor line, then hollow to an even wall built inwards. The colours show the wall thickness.
Anvil.Health check: Open any STL car and Anvil tells you what kind of model it is, how thick its walls are and what needs fixing.
Anvil.Chassis fit: Anvil finds the wheel arches and suggests a chassis that fits, shown with its tyres inside the body.
Anvil.Race numbers: Race numbers in your own fonts, raised on both doors and following the curve of the body.
Anvil.Glue tabs: Slice the body in two to print it in parts. Glue tabs, shown in amber, help the pieces line up.
Anvil.Interior: A cockpit tray with a driver and steering wheel, shaped to the side walls and shown in amber first.
Anvil.Posts and tabs: Screw posts reach from the chassis deck into the wall; tabs on the side walls hold the body too.
Anvil.Final check: One list of everything that matters before printing, each with a button to the tool that fixes it.

Frame.Select and drag in 3D: Click a part in 3D to open its settings, then move it with the orange handles. A position reference keeps it in place when the wheelbase changes.
Frame.Rear wings: Start from a GT3 swan neck, LMP, DTM, Group C or classic wing, and see it from behind and from the side with its legs and pins.
Frame.Inserts on the car: The wheel inserts sit in the car’s wheels in 3D, with the body from Anvil round them, while you try designs.
Frame.Clearance inspection: A section along the car shows the chassis inside the body, and the smallest gap between them is measured on the real solids.
Frame.Arrange features: Duplicate, move, mirror, align and space out ribs and other features, and keep them together as a named group.
Frame.Wheel inserts: Design an insert for an aluminium wheel from layers, or pick one of ten ready-made designs by Jivko Design.
Frame.Peter’s 1:43 Chassis: A one-piece 1/43 chassis with the motor in the chassis itself. Every size can be changed, and Back to Peter’s puts them back.
Frame.Bearings and bushings: Flanged bearings and bushings, with the flange on the wheel side, the motor side or both, sunk into the upright or standing out.
Frame.Final check: One list of everything that matters before you print. Here positions count from the rear axle, marked by a red 0.
